tool_config.name: focus_region
tool_config.description: Bring a problem into view on the board. Use it before talking about a problem the student can't currently see.

region_id.description: ID of a homework region exactly as listed, such as p1.q3, or of a question you wrote, such as q1.

tool_config.name: point_at
tool_config.description: Point at a problem with your pen, without leaving a mark. Use it as you say "look here".

region_id.description: ID of a homework region exactly as listed, such as p1.q3, or of a question you wrote, such as q1.

tool_config.name: circle_region
tool_config.description: Circle a problem by hand in your color, while you start talking about it. Good for naming what's being asked.

region_id.description: ID of a homework region exactly as listed, such as p1.q3, or of a question you wrote, such as q1.

tool_config.name: underline_region
tool_config.description: Underline a problem by hand. Good for the facts that matter in a word problem.

region_id.description: ID of a homework region exactly as listed, such as p1.q3, or of a question you wrote, such as q1.

tool_config.name: highlight_region
tool_config.description: Highlight a problem with a marker. Good for the part the student should focus on.

region_id.description: ID of a homework region exactly as listed, such as p1.q3, or of a question you wrote, such as q1.

tool_config.name: draw_arrow
tool_config.description: Draw an arrow between two problems or questions to show how they relate.

from_region_id.description: ID the arrow starts at: a region such as p1.q3, or a question such as q1.

label.description: Optional short label for the arrow, a few words at most.

tool_config.name: write_text
tool_config.description: Write a short hint in your handwriting beside a problem. Hints only, never a final answer.

near_region_id.description: ID of the homework region, or of your question (such as q1), that this belongs beside.

text.description: The hint, a few words in the session's language.

tool_config.name: write_math
tool_config.description: Write a short equation beside a problem, as a hint step. Never a final answer.

near_region_id.description: ID of the homework region, or of your question (such as q1), that this belongs beside.

latex.description: The equation as LaTeX, such as \frac{3}{4} + x = 2. Never read this aloud.

tool_config.name: number_line
tool_config.description: Draw a number line beside a problem, with values marked. Use it for fractions, decimals, negative numbers, inequalities and comparing sizes.

near_region_id.description: ID of the homework region, or of your question (such as q1), that this belongs beside.

min.description: The smallest number on the line.

max.description: The largest number on the line.

marks.description: Optional values to mark, separated by commas, each as value or value:label, such as "1/2, 0.75:three quarters". At most 6. Never mark the final answer.

tool_config.name: ask_question
tool_config.description: Write a question or a practice problem on the board for the student to answer, with a box under it to answer in. Works with or without homework. It returns the question's ID, such as q1, for your other tools and read_student_work. After calling it, stop and let the student answer.

question.description: The question, short, in the session's language. Never include the answer.

near_region_id.description: Optional ID of the homework region to write it beside. Leave it out to write it on a free spot of the board.

tool_config.name: read_student_work
tool_config.description: Look at what the student has written on a problem, or in the answer box of one of your questions, and get a report on whether it's right. Use it when the student asks you to check their work, or when a message says they wrote an answer. It takes a few seconds, so say you're taking a look first.

region_id.description: ID of a homework region exactly as listed, such as p1.q3, or of a question you wrote, such as q1.

tool_config.name: clear
tool_config.description: Remove your own marks and questions from the board. The student's work stays. Use it when moving to a different problem.
